LanguageData.AB_BasementOreDensity: Basement ore density: {0} lumps per 10k cells
LanguageData.AB_LinkNeedsApproach: Must have at least one open cell directly beside it (not diagonal) for pawns to step in from.
LanguageData.AB_LevelNotDug: Nothing has dug into that level yet. Build stairs down to reach it.
LanguageData.AB_MapSizeBandedTip: As above, So below stacks {0} playable levels into a single map, so this colony costs the stacked cell count shown. That is the figure RimWorld's pathfinder works over, not the per-level size. These sizes are chosen to sit just under a 64-row boundary, where the dead space between levels shrinks to its 2-row minimum. Sizes in between waste up to a fifth of the map on empty seam.
LanguageData.AB_MapSizeLockedTip: Locked by As above, So below: this size across {1} stacked levels would exceed the {0} cell budget. RimWorld's pathfinder works over every cell of the whole stack, so the budget is what keeps a tall colony affordable. Either choose fewer levels, a smaller per-level size, or lift the budget in the As above, So below mod settings.
LanguageData.AB_UnclampConfirm:
You are about to remove the {0}-cell limit on stacked colony maps.
RimWorld rebuilds its pathfinding grid across EVERY cell of the map. A stacked colony is every level plus its gutters tall, so the cost is paid on the whole tower at once, not on the level you are looking at. Going past the limit can mean long freezes when pawns repath, multi-minute map generation, and save files that grow very large.
If you continue, you accept that colonies generated above the limit are UNSUPPORTED. Performance reports from these maps cannot be acted on, and the recommended fix will always be to start a colony within the limit.
You can turn this back off at any time; existing colonies keep the size they were generated at.
LanguageData.AB_BudgetExplain: The {0}-cell budget is fixed. It is chosen so the largest sensible layouts fit and the ones that cause freezes do not. Levels and per-level size are traded against each other on the colony creation screen.
LanguageData.AB_PathHeuristicTip: Raising this makes pawns on a stacked map search fewer cells when working out a route. They find their way just as reliably, but may occasionally take a slightly longer walk instead of the perfect one. Leave it off unless a large colony is stuttering when many pawns pick new jobs at once. Ordinary maps are never affected.
LanguageData.AB_ClimateNewColonyNote: Climate is fixed when a colony is generated. Changes here affect NEW colonies only. Your existing saves keep the climate they were made with.
LanguageData.AB_ClimateWindNote: Wind turbine output only. There is no wind below the surface.
LanguageData.AB_ClimateLevelTemp: Level {0}: {1} deg offset (surface now becomes {2} deg here)
LanguageData.AB_LevelsHeadroom: This size affords up to {0} levels
LanguageData.AB_LevelsNoneNote: No extra levels: this colony generates as an ordinary single-level map.
LanguageData.AB_LevelsDefault: New colonies: {0} above, {1} below ({2} levels). Choose per colony on the map size screen when starting one.
LanguageData.AB_NaturalPeaks: Naturalistic mountain peaks on new sky levels
LanguageData.AB_NaturalPeaksTip: Mountain tops on newly generated sky levels come out as walkable highland plateaus: natural terrain with patches of soil and vegetation, rocky outcrops, and a cliff rim of solid rock whose depth wanders naturally. Off restores the classic fully solid peak. Existing sky levels are unchanged either way.
LanguageData.AB_SettingsGenerationNote: Generation settings apply to NEW colonies only. Existing colonies keep the layout they were generated with.
LanguageData.AB_SkyBiomeInheritTip: Newly created sky levels use the same biome as the surface map below, so plateau soil, greenery, tree regrowth, wild plant mix, and weather match the world around the mountain - including modded biomes, whose own fertile terrain and plants carry up to the peak. Applies when a sky level is first generated; existing sky levels keep the biome they were created with. Off restores the stark high-altitude look.
LanguageData.AB_SubsystemDown: As above, so below: the '{0}' subsystem hit an error and shut itself down to protect your game. Other features keep running. You can re-arm it from the mod settings; details are in the log.
LanguageData.AB_SubsystemDownBecause: As above, so below: the '{0}' subsystem hit an error (likely cause: {1}) and shut itself down to protect your game. Other features keep running. You can re-arm it from the mod settings; details are in the log.
LanguageData.AB_UnclampMapSize: Allow colony maps beyond the {0} cell budget
LanguageData.AB_UnclampMapSizeTip: As above, So below stacks every level of a colony into one map, and RimWorld's pathfinder works over every cell of that whole stack. Layouts are therefore budgeted by total cells rather than by per-level size: more levels means a smaller affordable footprint each. {0} cells covers seven levels at 126x126, four at 190x190, or two at 254x254. Every offered layout costs roughly the same to run, so the choice is about the shape of your colony rather than its speed. Combinations that exceed the budget are locked unless you enable this.
LanguageData.AB_UnclampMapSizeWarning: WARNING: large maps will hurt performance badly. Unlocking this restores RimWorld's full size list, including sizes that fall badly on the 64-row boundary and spend up to a fifth of the map on empty space between levels. A 325x325 banded colony is roughly 300,000 cells for 317,000 of pathfinding work. Expect slowdowns and long map generation.
LanguageData.AB_VisualsNote: How looking down through a level at the ones beneath it is drawn. Purely visual and can be changed at any time; it does not affect generation, pathing or what your colonists can reach.
LanguageData.AB_DepthFalloffTip: Pawns, plants and loose items on a level below the one you are viewing draw slightly smaller, and smaller again for each further level down, the way anything further away looks smaller. This is the cue that makes a deep column read as depth instead of as flat levels stacked in a list. Buildings never shrink: a solar panel, a wall or a workbench keeps its true size at every depth, so it always matches the floor it is standing on.
LanguageData.AB_DepthFalloffAmount: Size per level down: {0} (three levels down: {1})
LanguageData.AB_BelowPawnCacheAutoTip: RimWorld can draw a person from a small prerendered image instead of rebuilding them from body, clothes and wounds every single frame. It is much faster, and it looks identical right up until that image has fewer pixels than your screen is showing, at which point the person would start to look soft. This setting works out where that point is for your monitor and your current zoom, and uses the fast version only on the near side of it. People on lower levels are already drawn smaller, so they reach it sooner. On most displays that means every zoom level, with no visible difference at all.
LanguageData.AB_BelowPawnCacheAggressiveTip: Use the fast version at every zoom, including zoomed right in, where people on lower levels may look slightly soft compared to the ones on the level you are viewing. Worth it on a large monitor with a deep colony, where you are looking down several levels at once and want the frames more than the last of the detail.
LanguageData.AB_BelowPawnCacheOffTip: Always rebuild people on lower levels from scratch, every frame. This is the slowest option and looks the same as the recommended one in almost every situation. Use it if you suspect this feature of causing a visual problem, so you can rule it out.
LanguageData.AB_ClampZoom: Stop zooming out at the edge of the level
LanguageData.AB_ClampZoomTip: A level is a band of the map, not the whole of it, so once the view is as tall as the level there is nothing further out to see. Leave this on and the camera simply stops there. Turn it off if you use a camera mod that widens the zoom range and you would rather keep zooming out and see empty backdrop above and below the level. Either way the level next door never shows through.
LanguageData.AB_VerboseLoggingTip: Write detailed diagnostic messages to the log. Only useful when hunting a bug.
LanguageData.AB_ArrivalsMasterTip: Master switch. When enabled, raiders, visitors, traders and animals can walk onto and off the map via levels other than the surface, governed by the toggles below. When disabled, everyone arrives and leaves on the surface, as before. Safe to change mid-game; it applies from the next arrival or departure.
LanguageData.AB_ArrivalsNote: A level can only host arrivals if it has open ground at the map edge and a connected route to your colony. How often a level is used scales with how much walkable map edge it has, so mountain ridges and dug-out tunnels matter more the bigger they are.
LanguageData.AB_ArriveUpperTip: Groups can walk in over ridge routes and high ledges, appearing at the map edge of a level above the surface.
LanguageData.AB_ArriveLowerTip: Groups can emerge from tunnel mouths, appearing at the map edge of a level below the surface. Note that raiders arriving underground bypass surface defenses entirely.
LanguageData.AB_LeaveUpperTip: Departing or fleeing groups may exit off the map edge of a level above the surface if that is their nearest reachable way out.
LanguageData.AB_LeaveLowerTip: Departing or fleeing groups may exit off the map edge of a level below the surface if that is their nearest reachable way out.
LanguageData.AB_GuardHealthNote: Each subsystem shuts itself down if it hits an error, so one fault cannot break the rest of the mod or your game. Tripped switches reset when a game is loaded or started. Re-arming gives the subsystem another chance; if the fault is still there it will trip again with a fresh report.
LanguageData.AB_WrongLevel: On a different level. Switch to that level to give orders there.
LanguageData.AB_StairsNoBands: This map has no levels; vertical links have nothing to connect.
LanguageData.AB_ViewLevelDesc: Jump the camera to this link's other end on level {0} and select it.
LanguageData.AB_StairsNoLevel: No level in that direction; this link connects nothing.
